goal: Wire the literal-user approval recording surface for Kernel canary tasks: /imm-canary-authorize <task-id> record-user-approval mints an exact-action user-kind capability after a fresh TUI confirmation and applies record_user_approval through the existing authority-bound application, so critical-risk tasks can reach completion without weakening the closed tool schema or privileged-action boundaries.

acceptance.assertion: The Pi TUI command /imm-canary-authorize <task-id> record-user-approval records a user-kind approval on the task record (phase review) through the exact-action capability path after a fresh ctx.ui.confirm; cancellation, timeout, abort, late confirmation, reentry, replay, and stale record/intent/diff state perform zero writes; the capability is consumed exactly once.

The extension builds the approval payload (kind user, authority_role user) bound to the fresh projection's task_revision, intent_content_hash, and diff_hash and mints a capability with authority_kind user and action_kind record_user_approval; the reducer record_user_approval path requires kind user, user authority, phase review, matching revision/hash/diff, and rejects duplicate approval ids; userOperationFor returns the record_user_approval op; the imm_kernel_canary tool schema remains closed to record_user_approval as an ordinary op.

A critical-risk canary task with fresh evidence for every acceptance id and fresh qa+review+user approvals is eligible for completion: completionDecisionV2 reports complete=true and the complete action transitions review to done with the task tombstone, released workspace pointer, and removed active claim.

dist/imm-canary-work.md and the skills shim document the record-user-approval wiring and its TUI-only exact-action confirmation semantics; package.json imports/exports and the .pi-extension entry manifest stay unchanged; no new privileged CLI, RPC, JSON, or print route exposes user approval recording; README describes user-kind approval for critical tasks.
